head: Tahar Ben Ammar
note: Negotiated and signed the independence protocol of 20 March 1956, and continued as first head of government of the independent Kingdom from 20 March until the handover to Bourguiba on 11 April 1956. Included for continuity with the protectorate elite; flagged `pre_independence` so it can be excluded from the post-independence analysis frame.

head: Habib Bourguiba
note: First government of independent Tunisia, formed under the monarchy of Lamine Bey. Ends with the proclamation of the Republic on 25 July 1957. SOURCES DIFFER ON THE START DATE: Bourguiba was appointed Prime Minister by the Bey on 11 April 1956, but the government's composition was announced on 15 April. The later date is used because the unit of this table is the GOVERNMENT, not the person's appointment; the four-day gap after TN-00 is the real interregnum, not a data error.

head: Habib Bourguiba
note: Between the proclamation of the Republic and the appointment of a Prime Minister in November 1969, Bourguiba was simultaneously head of state and head of government; cabinet members held the rank of secretary of state ("secrétaire d'État"). Sources differ on how many numbered governments to distinguish in this period (at minimum a new composition was formed after Bourguiba's election as president on 8 November 1959). The harvester resolves the numbered cabinets and their reshuffles from Wikipedia rather than freezing one convention here.

head: Hédi Nouira
note: Appointed interim Prime Minister on 9 October 1970 while Ladgham was in Cairo; initial composition announced 6 November 1970.

head: Mohamed Mzali
note: Named coordinator of government action on 1 March 1980 before his formal appointment as Prime Minister on 23 April.

head: Zine El Abidine Ben Ali
note: Prime Minister for five weeks before deposing Bourguiba on 7 November 1987.

head: Mohamed Ghannouchi
note: Longest-serving Prime Minister. Remained in office across the 14 January 2011 rupture, forming two short-lived post-revolution governments (17 and 27 January 2011) before resigning on 27 February 2011. The `spans_regime_change` flag matters for era coding: appointments under this spell must be split at 2011-01-14 when era is assigned.

head: Hamadi Jebali
note: First troika government after the 2011 Constituent Assembly election.

head: Mehdi Jomaa
note: Technocratic government produced by the National Dialogue.

head: Youssef Chahed
note: Carthage Agreement government; several major reshuffles.

head: Hichem Mechichi
note: Dismissed by President Saïed on 25 July 2021; the office remained vacant until Bouden's appointment on 11 October 2021.

head: Najla Bouden
note: First woman to head a Tunisian government.

head: Sara Zaafarani
note: Second woman to head a Tunisian government; minister of equipment and housing before her appointment. `end: null` means incumbent as of the snapshot date recorded in data/processed/MANIFEST.json.
